stocks.value: 17.3× trailing earnings; Q2 Google Services revenue grew 15%, while trailing-12-month free cash flow was $53.3bn despite elevated AI investment.
stocks.thesis: Search, YouTube and Cloud form a highly profitable ecosystem; Cloud revenue grew 82% in Q2 and the company retains substantial liquidity.
stocks.risk: AI could weaken search economics; antitrust remedies and heavy infrastructure spending may reduce returns.
stocks.entry: $320–350, provided Search remains resilient and AI capital spending does not structurally depress free cash flow.

stocks.value: 15.8× trailing earnings, a compressed multiple for a high-margin subscription software business; Q2 revenue grew 13% to $6.62bn.
stocks.thesis: Creative Cloud, Document Cloud and embedded AI workflows support recurring revenue, pricing power and durable cash generation.
stocks.risk: Generative-AI competitors may commoditise content creation and weaken seat growth or pricing.
stocks.entry: $255–280, with a margin of safety only if recurring-revenue growth remains durable.

stocks.value: 18.4× trailing earnings; fiscal-Q3 automotive and IoT revenue grew 28% combined, while the licensing business remains strongly cash-generative.
stocks.thesis: Patent royalties fund diversification into automotive, industrial IoT, edge AI and data-centre computing.
stocks.risk: Apple modem insourcing, handset cyclicality and ambitious diversification investments could pressure earnings.
stocks.entry: Prefer $145–160, or wait for evidence that non-handset growth offsets Apple-related revenue losses.

stocks.value: About 11.6× the midpoint of raised 2026 adjusted-EPS guidance of $7.90–$8.10; first-half operating cash flow was $10.6bn.
stocks.thesis: The integrated insurance, pharmacy and benefits platform offers scale, recurring healthcare demand and recovery potential.
stocks.risk: Medical-cost inflation, regulation and leverage could prevent insurance-margin recovery.
stocks.entry: Below $92, or no more than roughly 11× sustainable adjusted earnings after confirming margin improvement.

stocks.value: 19.0× trailing earnings after depressed results; Q2 adjusted operating profit was $2.1bn and the Amazon volume reduction creates a possible earnings-recovery setup.
stocks.thesis: A difficult-to-replicate global network can regain operating leverage as restructuring and network automation mature.
stocks.risk: Weak parcel demand, labour costs and failure to rebuild volume or margins may make the apparent recovery value illusory.
stocks.entry: Prefer $90–100, or wait until two consecutive quarters show sustainable margin improvement.

note: Alphabet moves to rank 1 on the combination of a 17.3× earnings multiple, stronger recent operating growth and greater balance-sheet resilience; the other four names remain in the shortlist.
